rules.title: Job ads and career postings are not procurements
rules.rule_text: Job postings, hiring notices and career pages are not solicitations. Reject them as non-procurement content.

rules.title: Award notices and post-award documents are not open opportunities
rules.rule_text: Award notices, bid tabulations, executed contracts, purchase orders, modifications and commentary pages are not open solicitations.

rules.title: Health IT platforms are out of scope
rules.rule_text: Electronic health record, EMR, hospital information and telehealth/telemedicine software purchases are not Occu-Med services.

rules.title: Non-occupational health and facility services are out of scope
rules.rule_text: Health insurance and pharmacy benefits, veterinary/animal health, pest control, janitorial, landscaping, and food/nutrition programs are not Occu-Med services.

rules.title: Physical/IT work named in the title is not an Occu-Med purchase
rules.rule_text: When the title describes physical, facilities or IT work and names no Occu-Med service, medical wording elsewhere in the notice is contract boilerplate, not the thing being purchased.

rules.title: Safety consulting/training without clinical delivery
rules.rule_text: Treat as out of scope unless the notice also contains evidence of an actual Occu-Med service (see rescue terms). Safety consulting/training without clinical delivery.

rules.title: Background screening without medical/testing scope
rules.rule_text: Treat as out of scope unless the notice also contains evidence of an actual Occu-Med service (see rescue terms). Background screening without medical/testing scope.

rules.title: Drug testing adjacent non-workforce context
rules.rule_text: Treat as out of scope unless the notice also contains evidence of an actual Occu-Med service (see rescue terms). Drug testing adjacent non-workforce context.

rules.rule_text: Treat as out of scope unless the notice also contains evidence of an actual Occu-Med service (see rescue terms). Benefits/insurance instead of clinical employee medical services.

rules.title: Non-workforce medical screening
rules.rule_text: Treat as out of scope unless the notice also contains evidence of an actual Occu-Med service (see rescue terms). Non-workforce medical screening.

rules.title: Incidental contractor compliance requirement
rules.rule_text: Treat as out of scope unless the notice also contains evidence of an actual Occu-Med service (see rescue terms). Incidental contractor compliance requirement.

rules.title: Equipment/supplies rather than medical service delivery
rules.rule_text: Treat as out of scope unless the notice also contains evidence of an actual Occu-Med service (see rescue terms). Equipment/supplies rather than medical service delivery.

rules.title: Staffing and labor-supply procurements are out of scope
rules.rule_text: Staffing is out of scope for Occu-Med. Reject when staffing, clinical labor supply, locum services or ambulance operations is the purchased service. Words such as nurse, EMT, paramedic, firefighter or first responder do not trigger rejection when they identify the workforce receiving occupational-health services.

rules.title: Clinical treatment, pharmacy and plan administration without occupational exam scope
rules.rule_text: Patient treatment, pharmacy, cannabis and plan/claims administration are out of scope. Per Occu-Med policy an unlisted service is not automatically excluded, so these terms reject only when the notice has no occupational-examination or workforce-medical evidence (see rescue terms). Staffing is handled by rv_staffing_labor_supply.

rules.title: Benefit/disability adjudication and consultant panels are out of scope
rules.rule_text: Disability adjudication, benefit determination and medical-consultant panel work is claims/benefit adjudication, not employment fitness-for-duty. Consistent with the workers' compensation exclusion and IME policy.

rules.title: Unrelated technology, defense-materiel and fleet purchases
rules.rule_text: Satellite/Starlink, software licensing, IT, cybersecurity, ammunition and vehicle-maintenance purchases are not Occu-Med scope unless the notice also contains evidence of an actual Occu-Med service.

rules.title: Commodity and raw-material purchases are not Occu-Med scope
rules.rule_text: Bulk commodity, raw-material, fuel, metals and spare-parts purchases are not Occu-Med services. Applies to the notice title; a title that names an Occu-Med service term rescues it. Equipment-only purchases are covered by rv_cond_supplies_only.

rules.title: Informational wording without a procurement signal
rules.rule_text: Articles, blogs, webinars, definitions and how-to pages are informational content. When the notice also carries no procurement signal, lower its relevance (soft penalty, not a rejection).

rules.title: Job-title wording in the title without a procurement signal
rules.rule_text: A title that reads like a job title (nurse, technician, coordinator, assistant, director, manager) with no procurement signal is more likely a posting than a solicitation. Soft penalty, not a rejection.

rules.title: Network/managed-delivery scope needs service evidence
rules.rule_text: A provider-network or program-management notice counts as Occu-Med scope only when it also contains evidence of an actual occupational-health service (and a medical title).

policies.title: Judge the primary purchased scope, not incidental boilerplate
policies.instruction: Approve an opportunity only when the PRIMARY PURCHASED SCOPE requires occupational health, employee medical examinations, drug/alcohol testing, medical surveillance, audiometry, spirometry, respirator medical evaluation or fit testing, vaccinations, deployment medical screening, fitness-for-duty evaluations, or management of a provider network delivering those services. Reject records where medical, health, workforce, safety, testing or regulatory words appear only in clauses, background text, agency descriptions or generic boilerplate.

policies.title: Occu-Med must be able to bid
policies.instruction: Approve only when Occu-Med could realistically bid as the prime contractor or as a meaningful subcontractor.

policies.title: Understand semantic equivalents
policies.instruction: Treat these as equivalent to Occu-Med service language: workforce health, employee medical surveillance, pre-placement examinations, respiratory protection programs, audiometric conservation, deployment medical screening, occupational testing, and provider-network administration.

policies.title: Unrelated purchases to reject
policies.instruction: Reject construction, corrosion repair, painting, snow removal, parking garages, chillers, toilets, surveillance cameras, IT, laboratory equipment purchases, EEG systems, DNA extraction systems, weapons, facilities maintenance, treatment-only clinical care, general clinical staffing, insurance administration, grants, jobs and news, even when the notice contains incidental health or safety language.

policies.title: Commodity, raw-material and equipment supply is not Occu-Med scope
policies.instruction: Bulk commodity, raw-material, equipment and supplies purchases (for example metals, fuel, chemicals, drug-testing kits or laboratory supplies without a service component) are out of scope. A contractor-compliance clause such as maintaining a drug-testing policy does not make the purchase relevant. Canonical rule: rv_commodity_raw_material_supply.
